newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - TRW. CEO says China deal significant.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - TRW. CEO says China deal significant.

text.p: TRW Inc chairman and chief executive officer Joseph Gorman said Friday an agreement announced earlier for cellular telephone service in China is significant for TRW. He declined to give specific figures.
As reported, TRW is building the Odyssey satellite system through which cellular service will be provided in China.
"We hope to make a good deal of money on this deal," he said in a telephone interview. He said TRW expects to be able to reap "a return significantly above the cost of capital."
As reported, TRW and Canada's Teleglobe Inc jointly own Odyssey Telecommunications International Inc.
Gorman said Odyssey expects to announce additional equity investors later this year.

Odyssey, a patented $3.2 billion system using 12 satellites and seven ground stations, will begin service in 2001. ChinaSat, a unit of China's ministry of telecommunications, is the first service provider to sign on.

Developing nations are a key market and China's 1.2 billion people, most without telephones, make the China deal a milestone, Gorman said. Subscribers will be able to use pocket-sized mobile telephones or fixed wireless phones.
"This sort of system can revolutionize telecommunications and perhaps communications in much of the world," particularly regions with no telephone lines, he said.
"If I'm hiking in the Alps, even if there's no (communications) cell nearby, I can call you in your office" or a subscriber in remotest China once the system is operating.

China's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications and Odyssey signed a memo of understanding, which Gorman said is standard procedure for the China government and preliminary to a contractual agreement.
